paragraphs.title: The Sabbath Song, Gratitude, and Faith

answers: To give thanks unto the LORD
easy.explanation: The opening verse says it is a good thing to give thanks unto the LORD.
easy.q: What does the psalm say is a good thing?

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “It is a good thing to give thanks unto the LORD.”
easy.q: To whom should thanks be given?

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “To shew forth thy lovingkindness in the morning.”
easy.q: When is the LORD’s lovingkindness shown forth?

medium.explanation: The verse contrasts the morning with declaring God’s faithfulness every night.
medium.q: When is the LORD’s faithfulness declared?

medium.explanation: The passage mentions “the harp with a solemn sound.”
medium.q: Which instrument is mentioned in the passage?

answers: Stringed instruments and a solemn sound
medium.explanation: The psalm describes instruments of ten strings, the psaltery, and the harp.
medium.q: What accompanies the singing of praises?

answers: Sorrow in the morning and laughter at night
War in the morning and peace at night
challenge.explanation: The psalm says God’s lovingkindness is shown in the morning and His faithfulness every night.
challenge.q: What contrast appears in the passage?

answers: Worship includes thanks, singing, and instruments
challenge.explanation: The verses join giving thanks and singing praises with musical accompaniment.
challenge.q: What central idea connects thanksgiving and music?

challenge.explanation: The verse ends by addressing God as “O most High.”
challenge.q: How is God described in the opening verse?

paragraphs.title: The Greatness of God and the Downfall of the Wicked

easy.explanation: The speaker says, “thou, LORD, hast made me glad through thy work.”
easy.q: Through what does the speaker say the LORD made him glad?

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “O LORD, how great are thy works!”
easy.q: How are the LORD’s works described?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “When the wicked spring as the grass.”
easy.q: What do the wicked spring up like?

answers: The LORD’s thoughts are very deep
medium.explanation: The passage places the fool’s lack of understanding beside the depth of God’s thoughts.
medium.q: Why does the fool fail to understand the LORD’s works?

medium.explanation: Workers of iniquity are people who practice wickedness or evil.

answers: They will be destroyed for ever
medium.explanation: The verse says their flourishing leads to their being destroyed for ever.
medium.q: What will happen to the wicked despite their flourishing?

answers: God’s greatness versus the temporary flourishing of the wicked
challenge.explanation: The passage praises God’s greatness while showing that the wicked’s flourishing is temporary.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in this section?

answers: God is hidden only at night
challenge.explanation: The statement presents the LORD as supreme and eternal.
challenge.q: What does “thou, LORD, art most high for evermore” emphasize?

answers: They shall perish and be scattered
challenge.explanation: The passage says the LORD’s enemies shall perish and the workers of iniquity shall be scattered.
challenge.q: How are the LORD’s enemies described at the end of the section?

paragraphs.title: The Elevation of the Righteous and the Fall of His Enemies

answers: The house of the LORD being built
easy.explanation: The speaker says, “Mine eye also shall see my desire on mine enemies.”
easy.q: What does the speaker’s eye see?

easy.explanation: The passage refers to “the wicked that rise up against me.”

answers: They flourish like the palm tree
easy.explanation: The next verse says, “The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree.”

answers: He witnesses the defeat of his enemies
medium.explanation: The wording presents the speaker as seeing the outcome he desires concerning his enemies.
medium.q: What does the speaker’s eye seeing his desire suggest?

medium.explanation: The righteous are compared to a flourishing palm tree.
medium.q: What does the palm tree symbolize in this passage?

medium.explanation: The speaker describes seeing his desire concerning the wicked who rise against him.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the speaker and those who rise against him?

answers: The speaker’s enemies fall while the righteous prosper
The speaker becomes one of his enemies
challenge.explanation: The passage places the enemies’ defeat alongside the flourishing of the righteous.
challenge.q: What connection appears between the speaker’s vision and the righteous flourishing?

answers: The speaker personally witnesses the outcome
The speaker only hears a report
challenge.explanation: “Mine eye also shall see” emphasizes personal observation.
challenge.q: Why is the word “eye” significant in the description?

answers: The righteous flourish while enemies are overcome
The speaker is silent while enemies sing
The righteous grow old while enemies flourish
challenge.explanation: The verses contrast the flourishing of the righteous with the speaker’s desired outcome for his enemies.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast in these verses?

paragraphs.title: The Flourishing of the Righteous and the Certainty of Divine Justice

answers: A palm tree and a cedar
An olive tree and a fig tree
easy.explanation: The righteous are compared to the palm tree and the cedar in Lebanon.
easy.q: What two trees represent the righteous?

answers: In the house of the LORD
easy.explanation: The psalm says, “Those that be planted in the house of the LORD.”

answers: Bring forth fruit and remain flourishing
easy.explanation: They “shall still bring forth fruit in old age” and be flourishing.
easy.q: What do they do in old age?

medium.explanation: The tree images portray the righteous as strong, stable, and flourishing.
medium.q: What do the palm tree and cedar suggest about the righteous?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes continued productivity even in old age.
medium.q: What does “bring forth fruit” mean in this context?

answers: To show that the LORD is upright
To avoid the house of God
medium.explanation: The final verse says their flourishing shows that the LORD is upright.
medium.q: What is the purpose of the righteous person’s flourishing?

answers: Belonging to the LORD is connected with lasting growth
Being near the LORD prevents growth
challenge.explanation: The passage links being planted in the LORD’s house with flourishing and continued fruitfulness.
challenge.q: What connection is made between being planted in the LORD’s house and flourishing?

answers: He is upright and without unrighteousness
He changes and cannot be trusted
challenge.explanation: The LORD is called upright, a rock, and one in whom there is no unrighteousness.
challenge.q: What does the final verse teach about the LORD?

answers: As a faithful rock without unrighteousness
As a ruler needing help from sinners
As one who cannot be understood
challenge.explanation: The conclusion says, “he is my rock, and there is no unrighteousness in him.”
challenge.q: How does the psalm conclude its description of God?
